> **The keystone finding.** A real runaway is *distributed across agents with rotating/absent run-ids*, so any per-run cap goes blind. Argus's load-bearing control is therefore the **armed, durable, rotation-proof per-principal backstop** — control anchored to the one thing an agent can't forge (its authenticated principal). Per-run / per-conversation caps are the fast, precise early catches; the backstop is what actually *holds*. This is "controlling the agent" made concrete against an agent that tries to evade control.

Based on the landscape doc, the six per-area designs, and their adversarial critiques, here is the reconciled, build-ready design doc. The dominant cross-cutting blocker — repeated in all six critiques — is that the canonical $47K loop is **distributed across ~4 agents with rotating or non-shared run-ids**, while every invariant and pattern was scoped per-run, so the whole system goes blind. The synthesis fixes this with a **three-axis identity model + an armed, durable per-principal backstop on a single Redis slot**, and threads that fix through every section.

---

# Argus v0.1 — Design Doc

Status: design-spike output, ready to scaffold against (build plan §11). License: Apache-2.0. Grounding: LiteLLM `main` (max_iterations_limiter.py, max_budget_per_session_limiter.py, parallel_request_limiter_v3.py, cost_calculator.py, model_prices_and_context_window.json), agentgateway/Solo.io reserve-then-settle kill-switch, Envoy `ext_proc.proto` / `processing_mode.proto`, OpenAI Chat/Responses + function-calling, Anthropic Messages + streaming SSE, OTel GenAI semconv, GEP-713/2648/2649. Where a claim is design-by-analogy rather than copied, it is marked **(analogy)**.

Two correction notes that propagate from the critiques and are accepted as ground truth here:
- **Reserve-then-settle is agentgateway's shape, NOT LiteLLM's.** LiteLLM is check-then-accumulate (blocks the *next* call on already-committed spend). Argus adopts agentgateway's reserve-then-settle and says so.
- **LiteLLM's run identity is client-supplied `metadata.session_id`** — therefore untrusted and rotatable. Argus never treats a caller-supplied id as a trust anchor.

---

## 1. Overview & The One Decision Model

### 1.1 The single contract everything hangs off

Detection logic lives in exactly **one** place: one atomic Redis Lua script (`decide.lua`) behind one Go method `Engine.Decide`. Every Tap (standalone proxy, LiteLLM hook, ext_proc) is a *translator only* — wire bytes ⇄ `engine.Request`/`engine.Decision`. No Tap re-implements an invariant; this is the structural reason the three Taps cannot drift.

```go
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
package engine

// Request is transport-agnostic; every Tap fills it identically.
type Request struct {
    // --- identity (resolved server-side; see §2). The 3 axes. ---
    Principal    string // UNFORGEABLE trust anchor (auth-key hash / JWT sub / SPIFFE). Never a raw caller header.
    Conversation string // cross-agent run-graph correlation (propagated or content-derived). Namespaced.
    RunID        string // finest per-invocation scope; caller-influenced.
    PrincipalOK  bool   // false => principal could not be authenticated (empty/absent cred)

    // --- payload, OTel-GenAI-aligned ---
    Provider  Provider // OpenAIChat | OpenAIResponses | Anthropic
    Model     string   // gen_ai.request.model
    CallID    string   // SERVER-MINTED uuid; idempotency key for EVAL retry + Settle
    TurnDepth int      // # of prior assistant/tool turns in the replayed history (dedup anti-false-positive)

    // --- fingerprints (computed by the shared canonicalizer, §3) ---
    PromptHash string   // dedup invariant (input leg)
    Actions    []Action // emitted/replayed tool calls (RecursionLoop, action leg)

    // --- cost (§5) ---
    EstInputTokens int64
    MaxOutTokens   int64 // req.max_tokens or model default; drives the reservation
    HasServerTools bool  // tools[] present => reserve headroom for tool re-injection
}

type Decision struct {
    Allow     bool
    Reason    Reason   // OK | StepCap | Budget | Duplicate | RecursionLoop | RetryStorm | RateSpike | EngineUnavailable
    Scope     Scope    // Run | Conversation | Principal  (which axis tripped)
    Invariant string   // stepCap | budgetUSD | inputHashDedup | <pattern>
    Mode      Mode     // Enforced | DryRun | FailOpen | FailClosed
    Retry     time.Duration // 0 => terminal (non-retryable); >0 => Retry-After
    Detail    string
}

type Usage struct { // post-call truth for Settle
    InputTokens, OutputTokens, CacheReadTokens, CacheCreationTokens int64
    ServerToolCalls map[string]int64 // e.g. {"web_search":1}
}

type Engine interface {
    Decide(ctx context.Context, r Request) Decision   // hot path; ONE EVALSHA; NEVER returns error (folds failure into Decision)
    Settle(ctx context.Context, r Request, u Usage)    // off hot path; idempotent by CallID; clamps to outstanding reserve
}
```

`Decide` never returns a Go `error`; fail-open/closed is resolved *inside* the engine wrapper, so the three Taps cannot diverge on failure behavior.

### 1.2 The One Decision Model: layered scope, not one magic guard

The hard lesson from every critique: **no single mechanism stops the canonical loop, because the loop is engineered (or accidentally arranged) to break whatever single key you scope on.** So Argus enforces every invariant at up to three scopes simultaneously, in increasing order of forgeability:

| Scope | Key axis | Forgeable? | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Run** | `RunID` | trivially (rotate per call) | low-latency convenience; precise per-invocation caps when ids are honest |
| **Conversation** | `Conversation` | only by changing actual content lineage | correlates an A2A multi-agent graph when ids propagate OR content is derivable |
| **Principal** | `Principal` | only by stealing another credential | **the load-bearing guarantee** — armed, durable, rotation-proof backstop |

The per-run and per-conversation caps are *early, cheap, precise* catches. The **per-principal backstop is the thing that actually holds** when an agent rotates ids, omits ids, injects nonces, or splits across agents. It is **armed by default** (has real thresholds), **durable** (cumulative over a rolling window, not reset by a 1h TTL), and may **fail-closed independently** of the global fail-open posture.

### 1.3 Reconciliation summary (what changed vs the per-area drafts)

1. **Three-axis identity replaces two-axis.** Adds an explicit `Conversation` axis and **arms** the principal backstop with first-class thresholds (`spec.backstop`). (fixes run-identity blockers 1, 9; cost blockers 1–2; crd blocker 1; engine blockers 1–2)
2. **Everything for one principal lives on one Redis hash-tag slot** `{p:<principal>}` ⇒ one atomic `EVALSHA`, no CROSSSLOT. (fixes engine blocker 3)
3. **Cumulative counters are durable** (refreshed-idle TTL capped by absolute `maxAge`), and a **sticky tombstone** survives counter expiry — a kill cannot be resurrected by a TTL reset. SHARED across step/budget/dedup. (fixes patterns blocker 3; cost blocker 5; crd blocker 2)
4. **Dedup is content-derived, depth-aware, threshold-based, principal+conversation-scoped, request-scan-primary, default-shadow.** (fixes dedup blockers 1–4; engine blockers 4, 7)
5. **Cost: reserve-then-settle (agentgateway), per-conversation+principal aggregate, idempotent settle, unpriced-model = ceiling-price, Anthropic input recomputed per-delta, server-tool fees priced.** (fixes cost blockers 1–8)
6. **Patterns repositioned: RetryStorm = transport-retry detector; RateSpike baseline excludes the short window + absolute ceiling; slow ramp is owned by the cumulative backstop, not by a window detector.** (fixes patterns blockers 1–2)
7. **Principal is never a raw caller header; refuse to resolve from empty auth; server-mint `CallID`.** (fixes run-identity blockers 2, 5; engine blocker 9)
8. **Block is terminal: `action: TerminateRun|Quarantine` writes a tombstone so a retrying framework gets a hard, non-retryable deny — the kill does not convert into a RetryStorm.** (fixes crd blocker 5; cost blocker 6)

## 2. Run Identity

### 2.1 Three axes, resolved server-side

```
RESOLVE(req, policy) -> {principal, conversation, runId, sources}

# AXIS 1 — principal (UNFORGEABLE). Resolved ONLY from gateway-authenticated signal.
principal, principalOK := resolvePrincipal(req, policy.principal)
  ordered, first non-empty:
    litellmAgentId/teamId  (LiteLLM user_api_key_dict — server-validated)
    jwtClaim:sub           (Envoy-validated JWT; ext_proc reads dynamic metadata)
    spiffe/mTLS peer id    (ext_proc downstream cert)
    apiKeyHash = sha256(validated downstream Authorization)[:16]   # bare proxy
  # X-Argus-Tenant is honored ONLY if policy.principal.from==trustedEdgeHeader AND the hop is
  #   an authenticated trusted edge that strips-and-reasserts it. NEVER read raw from the agent.
  if no credential present:        # empty Authorization, anonymous proxy hit
     principalOK=false
     => policy.principal.onMissing: reject (default for backstop) | degradeToConn | degradeToSourceIP
     # we REFUSE to hash an empty credential into a usable principal (that collapses all tenants to one constant)

# AXIS 2 — conversation (cross-agent correlation). Cooperative first, derived fallback.
conversation, src := firstHit:
   h:  X-Argus-Run-Id / X-Argus-Session-Id            (explicit; echoed on responses for A2A propagation)
   tp: traceparent W3C trace-id  = bytes[3:35] of the 55-char header (FIXED off-by-one)  validate full format
   ll: x-litellm-trace-id / x-litellm-session-id
   sx: X-Session-Id / X-Conversation-Id
   oc: body.conversation.id           (OpenAI Responses)
   pr: body.previous_response_id -> {p:<principal>}:resp:<rid> map   (opt-in; degrades to derived if store=false)
   md: body.metadata.session_id | conversation_id      (NOTE: bare run_id is DEMOTED — see 2.3)
   d:  DERIVED  = "d:"+b32(blake3(principal ‖ model ‖ normalize(firstUserMessage)))   # content anchor
       anchored by {p:<principal>}:seed:<b32> map under refreshed-idle TTL (survives turn boundaries)

# AXIS 3 — runId (finest scope). Same precedence but per-invocation; falls to derived-with-turn-bucket.

# EVASION GUARD — applies to ALL sources (NOT gated on isExplicit; fixes the derived-bypass blocker)
mintRate := ZADD {p:<principal>}:mint now (conversation||runId); prune; ZCARD over window
if mintRate > policy.evasion.maxNewRunsPerWindow
   OR cumulativeDistinctRuns({p:<principal>}:mint, longWindow) > policy.evasion.maxDistinctRunsPerDay:
      coalesce conversation := "p:"+principal      # the flood now shares ONE scope -> caps bite the aggregate
return {principal, conversation, runId, src, principalOK}
```

### 2.2 Header / field contract

```
REQUEST (Argus reads, in precedence)              RESPONSE (Argus emits)
  X-Argus-Run-Id  [alias X-Argus-Session-Id]        X-Argus-Run-Id: <conversation>     # cooperating orchestrator forwards to sub-agent
  traceparent (bytes 3..35 = trace-id)              X-Argus-Run-Source: <src>
  x-litellm-trace-id | x-litellm-session-id         X-Argus-Remaining-Steps / -USD     # per smallest configured scope
  X-Session-Id | X-Conversation-Id                  on block: 4xx + X-Argus-Decision: <terminal|retryable>
  body.conversation.id (Responses)                                + X-Argus-Reason: <invariant>:<scope>
  body.previous_response_id (opt-in map)
  body.metadata.session_id | conversation_id
  (Anthropic: no body session field -> header or derived; metadata.user_id -> principal/derived only)
  X-Argus-Tenant: honored ONLY from a trusted, authenticated edge hop
```

### 2.3 Evasion mitigations (the load-bearing part)

1. **Armed principal backstop (primary).** `spec.backstop.{budgetUSD,stepCap,window,failureMode}` (§6) gives the rotation-proof axis a real kill threshold and a **durable** rolling-window counter. Rotation degrades you from run→conversation→principal scope, **never to no-scope**.
2. **Mint-rate + cumulative-distinct guard on ALL sources** (including derived) — a nonce-injecting derived flood is counted as rotation and coalesced to `p:<principal>`. (fixes derived-bypass blocker)
3. **LangChain/LangGraph reality:** `RunnableConfig` mints a fresh per-invocation `run_id` UUID unless a `thread_id` is pinned — **organic rotation, no adversary.** Therefore bare `metadata.run_id` is **demoted below derived** and treated as a per-step id, never a run boundary; Argus prefers `thread_id`/`session_id`/`conversation_id`. Documented loudly. (fixes run-identity blocker 7 / crd evasion)
4. **`trust: derived`** anchors the conversation to `normalize(firstUserMessage)` — the agent cannot rotate it without changing its actual prompt.
5. **Cardinality cap** `evasion.maxActiveRunsPerPrincipal` (also a Redis-memory DoS guard; with `maxmemory-policy noeviction` mandated, §4) — overflow coalesces to `p:<principal>`.
6. **A2A is best-effort observability, NOT the kill path.** A non-cooperative orchestrator that doesn't echo `X-Argus-Run-Id` simply isn't correlated at conversation scope — and that's fine, because the **armed principal backstop is the cross-agent control.** Optional A2A-protocol-aware `contextId`/`taskId` parsing is a separate, non-default tap (Open Fork).

**Grounded vs fork.** Grounded: LiteLLM `metadata.session_id` read order + `{session_*:<id>}` hash-tag key shape + `x-litellm-trace-id` + `require_trace_id_on_calls_by_agent`; Anthropic's absence of a session field; OpenAI Responses `conversation`/`previous_response_id`; OTel "do not synthesize `gen_ai.conversation.id`" (why derived stays `d:`-namespaced and is emitted only as `argus.run.id`). Forks: §10.

## 3. Dedup & RecursionLoop

### 3.1 Two fingerprints, one canonicalizer (kept — it survived critique)

| Fingerprint | Over | Guards | Maps to |
|---|---|---|---|
| **promptHash** | inbound request (last user turn, depth-tagged) | identical re-issue / ping-pong | `inputHashDedup` invariant |
| **actionHash** | `(tool_name, canonical_args)` the model emits | model repeats the same tool action | `RecursionLoop` pattern |

Both are `sha256_128("argus.v1.<type>\n" + ...)` over a canonical string. **Domain-separation prefixes are mandatory** so types can't collide in Redis.

**actionHash pipeline (transport reconciliation):** OpenAI `function.arguments` is a JSON **string** → `JSON.parse` (or `{"__argus_raw__":trim}` on error); Anthropic `input` is already an **object**. Then **RFC 8785 JCS** (sorted keys, no whitespace, canonical numbers) so OpenAI string-args and Anthropic object-input hash identically. **Strip ephemeral ids** (`call_*`, `toolu_*`, `tool_call_id`, `tool_use_id`) — they regenerate every turn and would defeat detection. Exclude `model`.

**Added robustness (fixes JCS type/array-drift):** before JCS, **coerce numeric-string scalars to numbers** (`"5"`→`5`) and **sort arrays flagged unordered** via an optional per-tool arg schema. Golden tests across OpenAI/Anthropic/LiteLLM payloads including type-drift cases.

### 3.2 The dedup false-positive fix (was a blocker)

The drafted `lastUserTurn` dedup blocks **every** healthy multi-step agent: in a growing OpenAI/Anthropic conversation the last `role:user` turn (or the sticky original instruction, after skipping Anthropic `tool_result`-only user messages) is **identical** on turns 2,3,4… So `threshold:2` kills a benign 50-step agent at step 2.

**Fix — depth-keyed, threshold-based, advance-gated dedup:**
- Key the dedup counter on **`(promptHash, TurnDepth)`**, not `promptHash` alone. A healthy agent's identical last-user-turn recurs at *different* depths → no collision. A true stateless re-issue of the same standalone request recurs at the *same* depth → collision. (`TurnDepth` = count of prior assistant/tool turns in the replayed history.)
- Fire only when **the conversation did not advance** between occurrences (no new assistant/tool turn) AND the prompt repeats `>= threshold` times within the window. Default `threshold: 3` (not 2), to coexist with bona-fide retries.
- **Default `action: flag` (shadow)**, not block, until a benign-multistep corpus shows zero false kills; then operators flip to `block`. Ship a regression test: *50-step benign agent under one conversation id is NOT blocked.*
- **Scope: Conversation + Principal**, not Run — so identical inputs across rotated run-ids still collide on the principal axis. Dedup hashes live in `{p:<principal>}:hashes` and `{p:<principal>}:conv:<conv>:hashes` ZSETs (true sliding windows — the prose no longer calls the INCR path "sliding").

### 3.3 RecursionLoop rule + the cycle/nonce/parallel fixes

**RecursionLoop fires when the same `actionHash` occurs `>= threshold` within window `window`, scoped per conversation** (default `threshold:3, window:10 steps`; `mode: windowed | consecutive` where consecutive = LiteLLM's max-reruns-3 parity).

Fixes pulled from critique:
- **Cycle evasion (≥5 distinct templated actions each appearing ≤2×):** add a **total tool-call-rate backstop per conversation** (this is literally RateSpike on the action stream) and optional **near-duplicate clustering by `tool_name`** when args differ only in low-entropy fields. Exact-fingerprint RecursionLoop is documented as a *floor*, backed by RateSpike + the cumulative step cap.
- **Volatile-token blindness (timestamp/uuid/turn-counter — routine framework behavior, not just adversarial):** ship an **arg/text ignore-list knob** in v0.1 (`fingerprint.ignoreKeys: [timestamp, now, date, request_id, uuid, turn, step]`) plus a low-entropy-field stripper, AND emit **`argus_fingerprint_unique_ratio`** so operators can *see* when nothing ever matches (the silent-failure signal).
- **Parallel tool calls in one turn:** **de-duplicate identical actions within a single turn before incrementing** the cross-turn window — so a legitimate parallel fan-out of the same action doesn't self-trip `threshold:3` in one turn; RecursionLoop measures *cross-turn* repetition.
- **Pure-text A2A ping-pong (no tool calls):** RecursionLoop is **structurally blind** (no actionHash). Documented. Coverage falls to depth-keyed dedup + the cumulative step/budget backstop. The demo must not claim RecursionLoop coverage for text ping-pong.

### 3.4 Enforcement direction (was a blocker)

**Request-scan is PRIMARY (pre-call), response-parse is the counter.** The inbound request body replays prior `tool_use`/`tool_result` and history, so Argus reconstructs the loop count **from the inbound request and blocks BEFORE the costly generation** — a 429 on the request that *would* continue the loop. Response-parse (with streaming `tool_calls`/`input_json_delta` reassembled to a complete value before hashing) updates the counter for the *next* turn. This makes the kill preventive instead of leaking one full generation per detection.

## 4. Patterns & Redis Engine

### 4.1 Engine primitives (grounded vs analogy, honestly labeled)

- **Run/conversation detectors → sorted-set sliding LOG** (`ZREMRANGEBYSCORE → ZADD → PEXPIRE → ZCARD`), grounded in the redis.io rate-limit tutorial. Bounded by `stepCap`, exact.
- **Per-principal RateSpike → bucketed sliding-window COUNTER (HASH of time buckets).** **(analogy)** — closest real prior art is Cloudflare's weighted two-bucket sliding-window-counter; it is NOT the LiteLLM v3 idiom (which is a fixed-window single counter). Validated by its own tests, not by a borrowed citation.
- **`redis.call('TIME')` for "now"** — grounded in LiteLLM `parallel_request_limiter_v3`'s `CHECK_AND_INCREMENT_BY_N_SCRIPT`. This is the **multi-replica consistency mechanism**: every replica EVALs the same shard; time comes from the shard, not the caller — no clock-skew TOCTOU, no leader election.
- **One hash tag `{p:<principal>}` per principal** co-locates run + conversation + principal keys on **one Cluster slot**, so the multi-key script is atomic and single-round-trip. (This is the conscious CROSSSLOT resolution — see §7.3.)

### 4.2 RetryStorm — repositioned to what it actually catches

RetryStorm is a **transport-retry-storm detector** (httpx/SDK hammering a 429/5xx, sub-2s inter-arrival), **not** the A2A-loop detector. Default `window:10s, threshold:5, similarity: Normalized`. The `attemptID`=`CallID` (server-minted) is the ZSET member ⇒ **idempotent on EVAL retry** (re-adding the same member can't double-count) — a deliberate improvement over LiteLLM's non-idempotent INCR. Documented: the count is current-request-inclusive (ZADD-before-ZCARD acts as a cooldown); off-by-one pinned by test (`threshold:5` blocks the 5th attempt).

The slow agentic loop is **explicitly not** RetryStorm's job; it is the cumulative step/budget backstop's job (§4.4). Window guidance is documented: `window >= expected loop period`.

### 4.3 RateSpike — baseline fix + absolute ceiling

```lua
-- RATE_SPIKE (bucketed counter, baseline EXCLUDES the short window; + absolute ceiling)
local now = TIME_ms()
local cur = floor(now/bucket_ms)
HINCRBY key cur 1 ; PEXPIRE key ttl
-- one HGETALL pass, prune < baseline cutoff, sum sc (short) and bc (baseline-incl-short)
local base_only = bc - sc                                   -- FIX: remove self-contamination
local expected  = (base_only / (nBaseBuckets - nShortBuckets)) * nShortBuckets
if expected < minBaseline then expected = minBaseline end    -- cold-start guard
local fired = (sc > mult*expected) or (sc > absoluteCeiling) -- FIX: catch "high and steady"
```

RateSpike is documented as a **step-change detector**: it catches bursts, not slow ramps. The canonical days-long ramp ($127→$891→$6,240→$18,400/wk) is **invisible to any ratio detector by construction** and is routed to the cumulative budget/step backstop. Default `action: Warn` (anomaly false-positive cost), operators opt into `Block`.

### 4.4 The cumulative backstop (new, load-bearing)

A **long-horizon cumulative counter per principal and per conversation**, independent of instantaneous rate:
```
{p:<principal>}:cum:steps     int     rolling-window step count   (backstop.stepCap)
{p:<principal>}:cum:spend     int64   rolling-window nanoUSD      (backstop.budgetUSD)
{p:<principal>}:conv:<c>:steps / :spend                          (per-conversation cumulative)
```
This is what stops the slow ramp and the rotating/distributed loop. It is armed by default and may fail-closed (§8).

### 4.5 Redis key schema (all under `{p:<principal>}`)

| Purpose | Key | Type | TTL |
|---|---|---|---|
| principal cumulative step / spend | `{p:<P>}:cum:steps` / `:cum:spend` | int / int64 | refreshed-idle, cap `maxAge` |
| principal reservations (idempotent) | `{p:<P>}:cum:reserved`, `{p:<P>}:res:<callId>` | int64 | per-res sub-TTL + reaper |
| principal dedup (rotation-proof) | `{p:<P>}:hashes` | ZSET | sliding |
| principal RateSpike | `{p:<P>}:rate` | HASH(buckets) | baseline+grace |
| mint-rate / rotation detection | `{p:<P>}:mint` | ZSET | evasion window |
| **sticky tombstone** (fail-closed kill) | `{p:<P>}:tomb` | HASH scope→reason | `maxAge` |
| conversation step/spend/dedup | `{p:<P>}:conv:<c>:steps`/`:spend`/`:hashes` | int/int64/ZSET | refreshed-idle, cap `maxAge` |
| RecursionLoop | `{p:<P>}:conv:<c>:act:<actionHash>` | ZSET | window+grace |
| run step/spend | `{p:<P>}:run:<r>:steps`/`:spend` | int/int64 | refreshed-idle, cap `maxAge` |
| run birth (absolute age cap) | `{p:<P>}:run:<r>:born` | int (SETNX) | `maxAge` |
| derived-seed / resp-id maps | `{p:<P>}:seed:<b32>` / `:resp:<rid>` | string | refreshed-idle |

### 4.6 TTL correctness (was a blocker) + eviction (was a blocker)

- **SHARED engine invariant:** every counter uses **refreshed-idle TTL** (PEXPIRE refreshed on *every* write) **capped by an absolute `maxAge`** (default 24h). This **diverges from LiteLLM's EXPIRE-on-first**, which silently resets a kill-switch counter after 3600s mid-run. Binding on step/budget/dedup *and* pattern keys. Integration test: *a counter written past 3600s does NOT reset.*
- **Sticky tombstone:** once any scope is killed, `{p:<P>}:tomb` is written and checked first in `decide.lua`. A TTL expiry can never resurrect a killed run.
- **Redis-up-but-evicting is a silent failure.** Mandate **`maxmemory-policy noeviction`** (or a dedicated Argus logical DB where only self-GCing keys live); emit `argus_engine_degraded{reason=oom|eviction}` on OOM errors, not only on connection failure. Bound run cardinality per principal so rotation can't blow the keyspace.
- **HA Redis ≠ hard guarantee.** Honest bound: the guarantee is only as durable as Redis persistence/replication. Recommend `appendfsync everysec` minimum; accept a bounded reset window on async failover; optional `WAIT` for the kill-path writes. The marketing claim "we never let a runaway through" is unsupportable under a failover and must not be made.

### 4.7 Multi-replica / SPOF / L1

- Atomicity from the single `EVALSHA`, so engine replicas are **stateless and horizontally scalable**.
- **L1 DualCache is allow-path-confirming only:** L1 may *add* an early block (a per-replica local storm trips without waiting for Redis) but may **never allow-without-confirming** to Redis. So it reduces latency on the *block* path, not round-trips on the *allow* path. (Removes the contradictory "cuts Redis load" claim.)
- `SCRIPT LOAD`→`EVALSHA`, fall back to `EVAL` on `NOSCRIPT` (LiteLLM's registration pattern). Redis 8.8 / Valkey 8 `FUNCTION` is an equivalent option.

---

## 5. Cost Accounting

### 5.1 Shape: reserve-then-settle (agentgateway), nanodollar fixed-point, per-conversation+principal aggregate

- **Reserve-then-settle** (agentgateway's shape, **not** LiteLLM's): pre-call reserves a conservative worst-case; post-call settles exact and releases the reservation. This is what makes the budget block **proactively** and survive concurrency (N concurrent calls can't all pass a stale check-then-add gate). Corrected attribution.
- **Integer nanoUSD via `HINCRBY`**, not float `INCRBYFLOAT` — exact, no drift. `budgetUSD "10.00"` → `10_000_000_000` nUSD. Prices scaled `round(litellm_value*1e9)`.
- **Aggregate at conversation AND principal scope**, not just run (fixes the "concurrent runs share a budget but keys are per-run" contradiction). The authoritative cumulative accumulators are `{p:<P>}:conv:<c>:spend` and `{p:<P>}:cum:spend`.

### 5.2 Gate (admission ≠ reservation — fixes the deadlock blocker)

```lua
-- GATE  on {p:<P>}  ARGV: budgetConv, budgetPrin, worst, ttl, callId
-- check sticky tombstone first
if HGET tomb any-scope ~= nil then return {0,'Tombstone',scope} end
-- ADMISSION: a single in-flight call is admitted if ALREADY-COMMITTED spend < budget,
-- even if worst_case alone exceeds the remainder. Reservation is CLAMPED to the remainder.
local committed = spent + settledReserved
if committed >= budget then return {0,'BudgetExceeded',scope} end     -- already over => block
local reserve = min(worst, budget - committed)                        -- clamp; never deadlock a cheap first call
HINCRBY reserved reserve ; HSET res:callId reserve ; PEXPIRE ...
return {1,'OK'}
```
This removes the draft's deadlock where any call whose `worst_case` alone exceeded the remaining budget was permanently rejected (so a run could never start). Over-reservation now only throttles *concurrency*, never rejects a cheap first call. `MaxOutTokens` defaults to a **`p95` historical cap**, not the model's full 128k, when the client omits `max_tokens`.

### 5.3 Settle (idempotent — fixes the leak/double-count blocker)

```lua
-- SETTLE on {p:<P>}  ARGV: actual, callId  (idempotent)
if HGET settled:callId ~= nil then return spent end          -- already settled (at-least-once delivery safe)
local r = HGET res:callId or 0
local delta = clamp(actual, 0, <bounded>)                    -- clamp; never allow negative claw-back from a replayed/buggy tap
HINCRBY reserved -r ; HDEL res:callId ; HINCRBY spent delta ; HSET settled:callId 1
```
Per-reservation **sub-TTL + reaper** reclaims orphaned reservations if a Tap crashes between gate and settle. The Tap must **drain/settle even on client disconnect**; missing `usage` ⇒ settle the pre-call estimate (or fail per knob), never $0.

### 5.4 Streaming (the Anthropic-input correction is a blocker fix)

- **Anthropic input is provisional at `message_start`, NOT exact.** Verified against the SSE spec's `web_search` example: `message_start input_tokens=2679` grows to `10682` by the final `message_delta` as tool results are re-injected. **Fix:** treat input as non-final — **recompute cost from the LATEST `message_delta.usage` on every delta** (cumulative output is in `message_delta`; the grown input shows up there too). Reserve **headroom** when `tools[]` is present.
- **Server-tool fees are priced:** `CostNanoUSD` adds per-request `server_tool_use` fees (e.g. `web_search_requests`) from the price table — not token-only.
- **OpenAI:** intermediate chunks are `usage:null`; Argus **injects `stream_options.include_usage=true`** upstream (transparently — does NOT echo the extra usage chunk to clients that didn't ask) for an exact final reconcile, and self-counts output deltas as a best-effort mid-stream meter.
- **Mid-stream abort is clean and terminal:** emit a proper terminating SSE event + `X-Argus-Decision: terminal` (not a dropped socket), settle the emitted-so-far usage **marked estimated**, and **write the tombstone** so the framework's retry hits a hard non-retryable deny instead of being re-gated as fresh load (this is the budget↔RetryStorm coordination).

### 5.5 Cost engine + price table

```go
func CostNanoUSD(p Price, u Usage) int64 {
    return tier(u.InputTokens,  p.InPerTok,  p.InAbove200kPerTok) +
           tier(u.OutputTokens, p.OutPerTok, p.OutAbove200kPerTok) +
           u.CacheReadTokens*p.CacheReadPerTok +
           u.CacheCreationTokens*p.CacheWritePerTok +
           serverToolCost(p, u.ServerToolCalls)        // per-request tool fees
}
```
- **Usage normalization:** Anthropic `input_tokens` *excludes* cache (separate `cache_creation`/`cache_read`); OpenAI `prompt_tokens` *includes* cached (`uncached = prompt_tokens − prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`). One normalized `Usage` struct.
- **Price table:** vendor LiteLLM `model_prices_and_context_window.json` (MIT, Apache-2.0-compatible; 1.51 MB, ~2,784 entries) as **build-time seed**, projected to an 8-field `Price` struct (nanoUSD). **In-image pinned + ConfigMap override + weekly CI refresh PR with golden tests.** The projector **fails LOUD (CI red) on a missing expected field** — a zeroed price = a budget that never triggers. Never import LiteLLM at runtime; never live-fetch on the hot path.
- **Unpriced model (was a fail-open bypass blocker):** `unpricedModelPolicy: ceiling | block | allow`, default **`ceiling`** — assign a conservative high price so the cumulative cap still bites, preserving availability without giving a free bypass. (Setting `model: gpt-4o-x` no longer = $0.)
- **OTel:** budgets accrue on `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens`/`output_tokens`; emit first-class `argus.run.cost.usd` (OTel defines no USD metric) alongside `gen_ai.client.token.usage`-mirrored token metrics.

## 6. RunawayPolicy CRD (v1alpha1)

GEP-713 Policy Attachment shape (`targetRefs` + `PolicyAncestorStatus` with `Accepted`/`Programmed`). Inherited (GEP-2649) primary; Direct (GEP-2648) per-route override. **The `backstop` is a non-overridable ceiling** (a more-specific route policy can only *lower* it) — closing the "child route raises the cap" evasion until a full defaults/overrides wrapper lands in v1beta1.

```yaml
apiVersion: policy.argus.dev/v1alpha1
kind: RunawayPolicy
metadata: { name: agents-prod-guard, namespace: agents }
spec:
  targetRefs:
    - { group: gateway.networking.k8s.io, kind: HTTPRoute, name: agent-chat-route }
    - { group: "", kind: Namespace, name: agents }            # Inherited cascade (proxy/LiteLLM taps)

  # ---- identity (§2): unforgeable principal + cross-agent conversation ----
  identity:
    principal:
      from: apiKeyHash            # apiKeyHash | jwtClaim:sub | spiffe | litellmAgentId | trustedEdgeHeader:X-Argus-Tenant
      onMissing: reject           # reject | degradeToConn | degradeToSourceIP   (NEVER hash an empty credential)
    conversation:
      sources: [argusHeader, traceparent, litellm, sessionHeader, openaiConversation, bodyMetadata, derived]
      trust: explicit             # explicit | derived
      derived: { hashFields: [principal, model, firstUserMessage], seedTTL: 1h }
    evasion:
      maxNewRunsPerWindow: 20
      window: 1m
      maxDistinctRunsPerDay: 5000       # slow-rotation guard (cumulative, not just instantaneous rate)
      maxActiveRunsPerPrincipal: 1000
      onExceed: coalesceToPrincipal

  # ---- invariants. `scope` is the DEFAULT enforcement axis (default Conversation). ----
  scope: Conversation                   # Run | Conversation | Principal
  stepCap: 50
  budgetUSD: "10.00"                     # string ^\d+(\.\d{1,4})?$  (NOT resource.Quantity — avoids 10.50->10500m UX trap)
  inputHashDedup:
    enabled: true
    scope: [Conversation, Principal]     # rotation-proof
    key: promptHashByDepth               # promptHashByDepth (default) | fullMessages
    requireNoAdvance: true               # only count repeats when the conversation did NOT advance
    threshold: 3
    window: "0"                          # 0 = whole-run (run/conv TTL); or a duration (true ZSET sliding)
    action: flag                         # flag (shadow, default) | block   -- flip to block after corpus validation

  # ---- ARMED, durable, rotation-proof backstop (always on; non-overridable ceiling) ----
  backstop:
    budgetUSD: "100.00"                  # per-principal cumulative kill
    stepCap: 2000
    window: 24h                          # rolling cumulative window (durable; NOT a 1h reset)
    failureMode: Closed                  # backstop may fail-CLOSED independently of the global default

  # ---- patterns (§4). Each has a scope; RateSpike+RecursionLoop default ON at Conversation/Principal. ----
  patterns:
    retryStorm:    { enabled: true,  scope: Conversation, window: 10s, threshold: 5,
                     similarity: { mode: Normalized }, action: Block }
    rateSpike:     { enabled: true,  scope: Principal,    shortWindow: 10s, baselineWindow: 5m,
                     multiplier: "5.0", absoluteCeiling: 600, minBaseline: 20, bucket: 1s, action: Warn }
    recursionLoop: { enabled: true,  scope: Conversation, mode: windowed, threshold: 3, window: "10",
                     dedupeWithinTurn: true, action: Block }

  fingerprint:
    normalization: strict                # strict (NFC+newline+trim) | loose
    ignoreKeys: [timestamp, now, date, request_id, uuid, turn, step]   # volatile-token defense
    ignoreModel: false
    includeSamplingParams: false

  cost:
    unpricedModelPolicy: ceiling         # ceiling (default) | block | allow
    preCallEstimate: heuristic           # heuristic | exact (count_tokens/tiktoken; NEVER tiktoken for Claude)
    streamingAbort: true
    omittedMaxTokens: p95                # reservation cap when client omits max_tokens
    priceTable: { source: builtin, configMapRef: argus-prices }

  # ---- lifetime + behavior ----
  run: { idleTTL: 1h, maxAge: 24h }      # refreshed-idle, absolute cap (cumulative correctness)
  enforcement: Enforce                   # Enforce | Dryrun
  action: TerminateRun                   # Deny | TerminateRun | Quarantine  (TerminateRun writes sticky tombstone)
  failureMode: Open                      # GLOBAL default (locked). backstop above can independently be Closed.
status:
  ancestors:
    - ancestorRef: { group: gateway.networking.k8s.io, kind: HTTPRoute, name: agent-chat-route }
      controllerName: argus.dev/runaway-controller
      conditions:
        - { type: Accepted,   status: "True", reason: Accepted,   observedGeneration: 4 }
        - { type: Programmed, status: "True", reason: Programmed, observedGeneration: 4, message: "pushed to taps: proxy,litellm" }
  observedGeneration: 4
  blocksByReason: { BudgetExceeded: 2, StepCapExceeded: 1, RecursionLoop: 1, InputHashDedup: 1 }   # best-effort, non-authoritative
```

### 6.1 Go type sketch (deltas from the draft)

```go
// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
// +kubebuilder:validation:XValidation:rule="has(self.stepCap)||has(self.budgetUSD)||(has(self.inputHashDedup)&&self.inputHashDedup.enabled)||has(self.backstop)||(has(self.patterns)&&(has(self.patterns.retryStorm)||has(self.patterns.rateSpike)||has(self.patterns.recursionLoop)))",message="at least one populated invariant/backstop/pattern required"
type RunawayPolicySpec struct {
    TargetRefs []gwapiv1alpha2.LocalPolicyTargetReferenceWithSectionName `json:"targetRefs"` // MinItems=1 MaxItems=16
    Identity   IdentitySpec   `json:"identity"`
    // +kubebuilder:default=Conversation
    Scope      Scope          `json:"scope,omitempty"`         // Run|Conversation|Principal
    StepCap    *int32         `json:"stepCap,omitempty"`       // Min=1
    // +kubebuilder:validation:Pattern=`^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]{1,4})?$`
    BudgetUSD  *string        `json:"budgetUSD,omitempty"`     // string money, NOT resource.Quantity
    InputHashDedup *DedupSpec `json:"inputHashDedup,omitempty"`
    Backstop   *BackstopSpec  `json:"backstop,omitempty"`      // armed per-principal ceiling
    Patterns   *PatternSpec   `json:"patterns,omitempty"`
    Fingerprint FingerprintSpec `json:"fingerprint,omitempty"`
    Cost       CostSpec       `json:"cost,omitempty"`
    Run        RunLifetime    `json:"run,omitempty"`           // idleTTL + maxAge
    // +kubebuilder:default=Enforce
    Enforcement EnforcementMode `json:"enforcement,omitempty"`
    // +kubebuilder:default=TerminateRun

    // +kubebuilder:default=Open
    FailureMode FailureMode   `json:"failureMode,omitempty"`
}
type BackstopSpec struct {
    BudgetUSD *string `json:"budgetUSD,omitempty"`
    StepCap   *int32  `json:"stepCap,omitempty"`
    // +kubebuilder:default="24h"
    Window      metav1.Duration `json:"window,omitempty"`
    // +kubebuilder:default=Closed
    FailureMode FailureMode     `json:"failureMode,omitempty"` // independent of global
}
type Scope string // Run | Conversation | Principal
```
Status counters are labeled **best-effort / non-authoritative** (eventually-consistent Redis aggregates, not billing truth).

---

## 7. Engine Interface & 3 Tap Adapters

### 7.1 One Decide commit per upstream call (was a blocker for ext_proc)

The engine exposes two methods: a read-only **`Precheck`** (tombstone + cumulative-ceiling read; no mutation) and the single mutating **`Decide`** (the commit point: increments steps, reserves budget, runs dedup/pattern windows). **Every Tap calls `Decide` exactly once per upstream call** — this is the invariant that keeps quota identical across taps.

### 7.2 The three adapters

- **A. Standalone proxy (OpenAI + Anthropic, v0.1 first):** sees the full body (required for dedup/model/estimate). `Principal` from validated downstream auth; `CallID` server-minted; `PromptHash`/`Actions` from the canonicalizer. Block → provider-shaped error (`{"error":{...}}` / `{"type":"error",...}`) `429` (invariant) or `503` (fail-closed) + `Retry-After`. Settle from `usage.*`.
- **B. LiteLLM `CustomLogger`:** `async_pre_call_hook` builds `Request` (**`Principal` from `user_api_key_dict.team_id` server-side**; LiteLLM's client `metadata.session_id` is classified `TrustHeaderUnsigned` → feeds Conversation only, never Principal — fixes the copied-untrusted-identity hole) and calls the **same** engine (gRPC); on block raise `HTTPException(429)`/`503`. `async_log_success_event` calls `Settle`, reusing `kwargs["response_cost"]` (inherits LiteLLM's price table for free).
- **C. ext_proc gRPC:** `ProcessingMode{request_header_mode: SEND, request_body_mode: BUFFERED_PARTIAL, response_body_mode: STREAMED}`. **Header phase = `Precheck` (read-only)** for cheap early tombstone rejection; **body phase = single `Decide` commit** (so steps/budget are committed exactly once). Block → `ImmediateResponse{status:429|503, body, headers:{retry-after}, details:"argus:<reason>:<scope>"}`. **BUFFERED_PARTIAL truncation fix:** hash a **stable bounded slice** (last user turn + emitted tool args), not the whole prompt, so a truncated body doesn't destabilize the hash; set the buffer limit to cover realistic prompts and document partial-hash semantics. `failure_mode_allow = (policy.FailureMode == FailOpen)` keeps the two ext_proc failure layers (Envoy↔ext_proc, ext_proc↔Redis) consistent.

### 7.3 CROSSSLOT decision (conscious)

**Everything for one principal is tagged `{p:<principal>}`** → run + conversation + principal keys live on **one slot** → `decide.lua` is a single atomic `EVALSHA` even on Redis Cluster. Cost: a hot principal is a slot hotspot. Mitigated by L1 (block-path only) + the fact that a single principal's traffic is itself rate-limited. Optional `{p:<principal>:<shardN>}` sub-sharding (loses exact cumulative) is an Open Fork, not v0.1.

### 7.4 Unified identity contract

A **single `resolvePrincipal`/`resolveConversation` library** is shared by all three taps so the same logical caller maps to the same `principal` regardless of tap (no cap-splitting via tap choice). For ext_proc-in-a-namespace, the cumulative ceiling is keyed on `conversation`/`principal`, never on pod namespace alone (which would split a 4-agent graph into 4 tenants).

---

## 8. Latency, Failure Mode & Threat Model

### 8.1 Latency budget

- Engine-added **p99 ≤ 5 ms (low-load), hard ctx deadline 20 ms**, one `EVALSHA`. Rides on a hundreds-of-ms LLM call ⇒ ~1–2% add. **Publish a benchmark at target QPS** (the per-principal rate HASH `HGETALL`/`ZREM` is the hottest op and degrades exactly under the spike it must detect) — if Redis CPU bound, switch the rate path to a probabilistic/coarser-bucket window or shard the hot principal.
- Pooled, pipelined `EVALSHA`; process-local **circuit breaker** trips after N consecutive Redis failures → short-circuits to the fail-mode (no 20ms thundering herd).
- ext_proc `message_timeout >= 100 ms` (well above our 20 ms) so **our** deadline is the SLO, never Envoy's.

### 8.2 Failure mode

| | Redis down, FailOpen (global default) | Redis down, FailClosed (backstop / high-assurance) |
|---|---|---|
| brand-new/unknown run | allow (availability) | 503 + Retry-After |
| already-killed (tombstone) | **stay blocked** | stay blocked |
| unpriced model | `ceiling` price (still accrues) | block |

- **Global default fail-OPEN (locked), but the `backstop` fails CLOSED independently** — the one axis where open = unbounded loss. Honest doc: during a *full* Redis outage a brand-new runaway *can* slip on a fail-open policy; the kill-cache/tombstone only protects *already-detected* runs.
- **Kill continuity across replicas:** tombstones live in Redis (shared), so a kill is visible to all replicas while Redis is up. During a Redis outage, the per-replica kill-cache only covers runs that *that* replica saw; documented limitation. High-assurance tenants set `backstop.failureMode: Closed` and run HA Redis with `appendfsync everysec`.
- "Fail-open never means fail-silent": every fallback emits `argus_engine_degraded` + an `EngineDegraded` status condition + a structured log.

### 8.3 Threat model + mitigations (the consolidated evasion table)

| Evasion vector | Defeats (per-run only) | Argus mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Rotate `runId` per call | run caps | conversation + **armed principal backstop**; mint-rate coalesce on **all** sources |
| Omit ids → derived flood w/ nonce | run caps, derived id, dedup | mint-rate guard applies to derived; ignore-key list strips the nonce; principal backstop |
| LangChain default per-invocation `run_id` | run caps (no adversary) | `run_id` demoted below derived; prefer `thread_id`/`session_id` |
| Slow rotation under mint threshold (~9/min for days) | mint-rate | **cumulative `maxDistinctRunsPerDay`** + cumulative per-principal step/spend cap |
| 4 agents, distinct trace per A2A hop | conversation caps | principal backstop is cross-agent; A2A is best-effort observability only |
| Inject timestamp/uuid into prompt/args | both fingerprints | `fingerprint.ignoreKeys` + low-entropy stripper + `unique_ratio` metric |
| Cycle ≥5 distinct actions | windowed RecursionLoop | total-action-rate backstop + step cap |
| Pace just under every window | RetryStorm/RateSpike | cumulative budget/step backstop (rate-independent) |
| `X-Argus-Tenant`/virtual-key rotation | principal | principal is gateway-authenticated only; never a raw caller header; refuse empty cred |
| Shared upstream key, no client auth | principal collapses to constant | `onMissing: reject` (no silent hash of empty Authorization) |
| Unpriced model `gpt-4o-x` | budget | `unpricedModelPolicy: ceiling` |
| Pin one constant `CallID` to freeze RateSpike ZSET | RateSpike | `CallID` is **server-minted**, never from the wire |
| Replay/negative Settle to claw back budget | budget | Settle idempotent by `CallID` + delta clamped ≥0, ≤ outstanding reserve |
| DoS Redis into fail-open / eviction | kill-switch | `noeviction` mandate, circuit breaker, degraded metric; backstop fail-closed for high-assurance |
| 429 → framework retries (kill becomes RetryStorm) | the kill itself | `action: TerminateRun` writes tombstone ⇒ hard non-retryable deny |

### 8.4 SPOF

All mutable state in Redis ⇒ stateless engine replicas. Blast radius of a compromised engine is *deny-only* (a DoS), bounded by the global fail-open default + an `argus.dev/disable` panic annotation that bypasses the Tap. Counters are short-TTL and reconstructable; a failover that loses recent writes briefly *under*-counts (fail-open-ish), with the documented durability bound from §4.6.

---

## 9. Does it stop the $47K loop?

Canonical scenario (dev.to anecdote, treated as illustrative): **4 LangChain agents**, 2 actively ping-ponging "effectively the same" message; history grows each turn; pace ~9 calls/min; ramps over days to a large cumulative bill. Default config: `scope: Conversation`, `inputHashDedup.action: flag`, global `failureMode: Open`, `backstop` armed + fail-closed. Trace through each guard:

| Guard | Per-run scope | Per-conversation scope | Per-principal backstop |
|---|---|---|---|
| **stepCap (50)** | **MISSES** — each LangChain invocation mints a fresh `run_id`; every run sees 1 step | **CATCHES if** ids propagate OR the derived content-anchor stitches the agents (identical opening prompt → same `d:` seed) → cumulative steps cross 50 within minutes | **CATCHES regardless** — `backstop.stepCap: 2000` on `{p:<P>}:cum:steps` trips on the rotation-proof axis |
| **budgetUSD ($10)** | MISSES (per-run spend tiny) | CATCHES when stitched: `{p:<P>}:conv:<c>:spend` reserve-then-settle crosses $10; tombstone written; subsequent calls hard-denied | **CATCHES regardless**: `backstop.budgetUSD: $100` cumulative; fails **closed** so even a Redis blip over days can't silently bypass; `ceiling` pricing means an unpriced-model dodge still accrues |
| **inputHashDedup** | MISSES (run rotates; and growing history changes fullMessages) | depth-keyed promptHash on `{p:<P>}:conv:<c>:hashes`: identical bounced message at the same turn-depth with no-advance → fires at `threshold:3`. In default `flag` it *records + alerts*; flipped to `block` it kills early | `{p:<P>}:hashes` catches identical inputs even across rotated runs |
| **RecursionLoop** | n/a if text-only ping-pong (no tool calls → blind, documented); if tool-driven, fires on repeated `actionHash` at conversation scope after JCS + id-strip + ignore-keys | — | — |
| **RetryStorm** | does **not** fire (9/min is not transport-retry cadence) — correctly out of scope | — | — |
| **RateSpike** | does **not** fire on a slow ramp (ratio≈1) — correctly out of scope; the absolute ceiling catches a *steady-high* variant | — | per-principal absolute ceiling catches steady-high |

**Verdict: YES — but the guarantee is the armed per-principal backstop, not any per-run invariant.** The honest story: per-run caps are blind to this loop by construction (rotation + distribution + growing context). The **conversation scope** catches it *early and precisely* whenever ids propagate or the content anchor is derivable; the **durable, fail-closed per-principal `backstop`** catches it *unconditionally* — it is rate-independent (beats the slow ramp), rotation-proof (beats id churn), nonce-resistant at the spend axis (you pay real tokens regardless of fingerprint), and tombstone-terminal (the kill doesn't convert into a retry storm). The earlier drafts that scoped everything per-run did **not** stop this loop; this synthesis does, with the backstop as the load-bearing control and dedup/RecursionLoop/conversation-caps as faster early catches.

Caveat carried forward honestly: under a *full multi-day Redis outage* on a fail-open policy, a brand-new runaway can still slip until first detection — which is exactly why the backstop defaults to `failureMode: Closed`.

---

## 10. Open Forks for the Human (Song)

1. **`inputHashDedup.action` default: `flag` vs `block`.** Recommended default **`flag`** (shadow) until a benign-multistep-agent corpus shows zero false kills, then document the flip to `block`. The depth-keyed + no-advance fix makes `block` safe in principle, but corpus validation gates it.
2. **Backstop thresholds + independent fail-closed.** Recommended **arm by default** (`backstop.budgetUSD ~10× the per-conversation budget`, `stepCap ~40×`) and **fail-closed independently** of the global fail-open. This contradicts a pure "never block legit traffic" reading — needs ratification.
3. **`identity.principal.onMissing` default.** Recommended **`reject`** for the backstop path (refuse to score an empty/shared credential). Friction for naive single-key proxy users → they must issue per-team virtual keys or run behind a trusted edge that sets `X-Argus-Tenant`.
4. **`requireRunId` (LiteLLM `require_trace_id_on_calls_by_agent`).** Recommended **off** for adoption smoothness; rely on derived + backstop. On = forces id commitment but breaks naive SDK users.
5. **Derived seed composition + bucket/TTL.** `blake3(principal ‖ model ‖ firstUserMessage)`, `seedTTL 1h`. Whether to include the system prompt and the time-bucket length are empirical (run-merge vs run-split). Note the residual **collision risk**: templated multi-agent systems reuse identical opening prompts → two distinct concurrent runs collapse — partially mitigated by bucket, fundamentally inherent to content-derived ids.
6. **RetryStorm `similarity` for v0.1.** Recommended ship **Exact + Normalized + a cheap structural Fuzzy** (SimHash over the last user turn, single LSH band) — the draft's "cut Fuzzy" leaves Exact/Normalized trivially evaded by a content nonce. Full multi-band Fuzzy is post-v0.1.
7. **`previous_response_id` threading.** Recommended **opt-in** (extra Redis write/call, SSE parse to capture `response.id`, silent degrade to derived on `store=false`); consider skipping for v0.1 and leaning on derived for Responses traffic.
8. **A2A-protocol-aware tap** (parse JSON-RPC `contextId`/`taskId` → conversation). Recommended **deferred, non-default**; the armed backstop already covers non-cooperative A2A.
9. **Per-principal slot hotspot vs `{p:<principal>:<shardN>}` sub-sharding.** Recommended **single-slot-per-principal for v0.1** (atomic, exact); sub-sharding (approximate cumulative) only if a target-QPS benchmark shows a hotspot.
10. **InferCost interop vs compete** (carried from landscape §10.1): InferCost = cost-truth feed (DCGM) into Argus enforcement, or independent price-table budget? Recommended **independent price-table for v0.1** (build-time LiteLLM seed), interop later.
11. **Redis vs Valkey 8.x** for CNCF license neutrality — recommended **document both**, default Redis 8.8 in dev, Valkey-compatible (no Redis-Stack-only commands used).

---

## 11. Build Order Adjustments (deltas to the W1–W12 plan)

The design adds one structural concept (three-axis identity + armed durable backstop) and several correctness gates. Adjustments:

- **W2 (engine + identity):** expand from "define run identity (trace-id/header)" to the **full three-axis resolver** (`Principal` gateway-auth-only + `onMissing`; `Conversation` propagated/derived; `RunID`) **and** the **single `{p:<principal>}` hash-tag schema + sticky-tombstone + refreshed-idle-TTL-capped-by-`maxAge`** as a shared engine invariant. This is the linchpin — do it before any invariant. Add the **maxmemory-policy `noeviction`** requirement to the Redis wiring.
- **W3 (invariants 1+2):** implement step/budget at **all three scopes** with **reserve-then-settle (agentgateway shape, corrected attribution)** and the **armed `backstop`**. Add the integration test *"counter past 3600s does not reset"* and *"50-step benign agent not blocked."* Implement `unpricedModelPolicy: ceiling`. Coordinate the shared-counter TTL rule with whoever owns step/budget (now unified here).
- **W4 (invariant 3 + RecursionLoop):** implement **depth-keyed, no-advance, threshold, principal+conversation-scoped dedup**, **request-scan-primary**, the **canonicalizer with `ignoreKeys` + within-turn de-dup + JCS type-coercion**, and the **`argus_fingerprint_unique_ratio`** silent-failure metric. Default dedup `action: flag`.
- **W5 (patterns):** RetryStorm repositioned as transport-retry; RateSpike with **baseline-excluding-short-window + absolute ceiling**; add the **cumulative-backstop slow-loop detector** here (it's the slow-ramp owner, not RateSpike).
